# IvritSuite

> Free Hebrew worksheets, flash cards, dictionary, weekly parsha reader, and classroom tools for Hebrew learning and reading practice — for teachers and students.

Everything runs entirely in the browser. There are no accounts, no ads, and no server:
presets, settings and custom fonts are saved on your own device, and are backed up by
downloading a portable `.ivrit` save file. The whole suite installs as an offline PWA.
The interface is available in English and Hebrew. Content is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (material
incorporating PocketTorah audio is CC BY-SA 4.0).

This is the expanded version of https://ivritsuite.com/llms.txt — every tool with its full description,
how-to steps, and questions & answers.

---

## Hebrew Worksheet Generator

https://ivritsuite.com/hebrew_blend_generator.html

Generate printable Hebrew decoding worksheets, bingo cards, and vocabulary drills. Customize letters, vowels, and difficulty for emerging Hebrew readers.

### How to make a Hebrew worksheet (about 1 minute)

1. **Pick a practice type** — Choose 1-letter, 2-letter, or 3-letter blends.
2. **Select Hebrew letters** — Pick which Hebrew letters to include in the worksheet.
3. **Select nikkud** — Pick the Hebrew vowels (nikkud) to include.
4. **Generate the worksheet** — Click Generate Worksheet to build the page.
5. **Print or export** — Click Print or Export PDF to download the worksheet.

### Questions

**What is a Hebrew blend worksheet?**

A Hebrew blend worksheet pairs Hebrew letters with vowels (nikkud) so students can practice decoding syllables one, two, or three letters at a time. The IvritSuite generator builds these as printable PDFs or bingo cards.

**Are these Hebrew worksheets free?**

Yes. All worksheets generated by IvritSuite are free to use and adapt for non-commercial educational purposes under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

**Can I print the Hebrew worksheets?**

Yes. The generator outputs print-ready PDFs sized for standard letter and A4 paper, suitable for classroom handouts.

**Do the worksheets include nikkud (Hebrew vowels)?**

Yes. You can choose any combination of nikkud — kamatz, patach, segol, tzere, hirik, holam, kubutz, shuruk, shva, and the hataf vowels — for each worksheet.

**What ages is the Hebrew worksheet generator for?**

The tool is designed for emerging Hebrew readers — typically elementary students and adult beginners — but the difficulty is fully customizable for any level.

## Hebrew Word Lookup

https://ivritsuite.com/hebrew_dictionary.html

Browse and filter a Hebrew dictionary by theme, word length, part of speech, era, and letter position.

### How to look up a Hebrew word

1. **Search** — Type a Hebrew word in the search bar — with or without nikkud.
2. **Filter** — Or use filters to browse by theme, length, part of speech, era, or letter position.
3. **Open a word** — Click a result to view its full details.

### Questions

**How do I look up a Hebrew word?**

Type the Hebrew word (with or without nikkud) into the search bar, or use the filters to browse by theme, word length, part of speech, era, or letter position.

**Can I filter the Hebrew dictionary by part of speech?**

Yes. Filter by noun, verb, adjective, adverb, and other parts of speech, alone or in combination with length and era filters.

**Is the Hebrew dictionary free?**

Yes. The Hebrew word lookup is free under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; word data is sourced from Kaikki.org.

**Does the dictionary include modern and biblical Hebrew?**

Yes. Words can be filtered by era, including biblical, mishnaic, medieval, and modern Hebrew.

**Can I share my filtered view or take a tour?**

Yes. Click the Copy link button in the results toolbar to copy a shareable link that reopens your exact filtered view, and your last-used filters return automatically on your next visit. Click the Tour button in the header for a quick 7-step walkthrough.

## Hebrew Classroom Dashboard

https://ivritsuite.com/classroom_dashboard.html

Live Hebrew date, time, weather, and days of the week for classroom SmartBoards and projectors.

### How to use the Hebrew classroom dashboard (about 2 minutes)

1. **Set your location** — Open settings and set your location for accurate weather and Hebrew date.
2. **Choose panels** — Pick which panels to show under Display Options.
3. **Customize Hebrew** — Pick a Hebrew font and nikkud display style.
4. **Project fullscreen** — Click the fullscreen button to project to your SmartBoard.
5. **Save a preset** — Save your setup as a preset, or start from a Quick-start layout in the Presets panel.
6. **Use fullscreen quick controls** — In fullscreen, move the mouse to reveal quick controls for settings, timer, text, and video.
7. **Edit text on the board** — Click the pencil on the dashboard message to edit it in place.

### Questions

**What is the Hebrew classroom dashboard for?**

It displays the live Hebrew date, time, weather, and days of the week for use on classroom SmartBoards or projectors during morning routine and Hebrew instruction.

**Does the Hebrew classroom dashboard work on SmartBoards?**

Yes. The dashboard is designed for SmartBoards, projectors, and large displays. A built-in fullscreen mode and zoom control let you size content for any classroom screen.

**Is the Hebrew classroom dashboard free?**

Yes. The dashboard is free to use under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for non-commercial educational purposes.

**Can I project the Hebrew date for my classroom?**

Yes. The Hebrew (Jewish) date and the corresponding Gregorian date are shown live and update automatically each day.

**Can the classroom dashboard switch layouts by time of day?**

Yes. Schedule Sync lets you build a weekly grid — paint each class across your periods and days — and the dashboard reconfigures itself through the day with a live Now/Next display and a countdown.

**How do I keep the classroom display from going to sleep?**

Fullscreen keeps the screen awake automatically, or turn on Keep screen awake in Display Options where the browser supports it.

**Is there a guided tour of the dashboard?**

Yes. Click the Tour button in the top bar for a quick walkthrough, and first-time teachers get a setup card with one-tap starter layouts.

## Hebrew Flash Cards

https://ivritsuite.com/flash_cards.html

Interactive Hebrew syllable flash cards for reading practice.

### How to use Hebrew flash cards (about 1 minute)

1. **Choose letters per card** — Pick 1, 2, or 3 letters per card.
2. **Select letters and vowels** — Choose which Hebrew letters and nikkud appear.
3. **Set deck size** — Choose how many cards to include.
4. **Start the deck** — Click Start to begin the practice session.
5. **Reveal and mark cards** — Tap each card to reveal it, then mark right or wrong.

### Questions

**How do Hebrew flash cards help reading?**

Hebrew flash cards build automatic letter–vowel recognition, which is the core skill behind fluent Hebrew reading. Repeated short drills with nikkud help students decode unfamiliar words faster.

**Are these Hebrew flash cards free?**

Yes. The IvritSuite flash cards are completely free to use for non-commercial educational purposes under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

**Do the flash cards include nikkud?**

Yes. Every card displays Hebrew letters with full nikkud (vowel marks), and you can choose which vowels appear in your practice set.

**Can I customize which Hebrew letters appear?**

Yes. You can pick any subset of Hebrew letters and vowels and choose 1, 2, or 3 letters per card to match the student's level.

## Torah Trainer

https://ivritsuite.com/torah_trainer.html

Read the weekly Torah portion in Hebrew with toggleable transliteration, translations, vowel color-coding, trope-family clause coloring, cantillation marks, chanted-audio karaoke, and TTS. Copy the color-coded passage out as formatted text, or print classroom sheets that repeat the reference and clause-color key on every page.

### How to read the weekly Torah portion with Torah Trainer (about 3 minutes)

1. **Pick a parsha** — Choose a parsha from the top dropdown. The page defaults to the current week's parsha based on the selected reading schedule.
2. **Choose a layout** — Switch between side-by-side (Hebrew + translation columns) and interlinear (stacked rows per verse). Toggle transliteration and translation independently.
3. **Customize appearance** — Open settings to pick a Hebrew font, color-code nikkud per vowel, and choose a transliteration scheme (Modern Israeli, Ashkenazi, SBL, Brill, or Simple Stressed).
4. **Listen and chant along** — Enable karaoke in settings, then pick an aliyah from the Reading dropdown. PocketTorah audio streams on demand and highlights each word as it's chanted.
5. **Project fullscreen** — Click the fullscreen button to expand the reading area for SmartBoard projection or focused study.
6. **Take it away** — Copy the passage as color-coded rich text for a handout, or print it — every printed sheet repeats the reading's reference and the clause-color key.

### Questions

**What is the Torah Trainer?**

A free Hebrew Torah reader. Pick a parsha and read it with optional transliteration, English translation, per-vowel color coding, cantillation strip, prose TTS, and chanted-audio karaoke that highlights words in time with the recording. When you are done reading, copy the passage out as formatted text or print it as a classroom sheet.

**Does Torah Trainer include chanted-audio karaoke?**

Yes. PocketTorah's recordings of all 54 parshiyot and their haftarot stream on demand, with word-level highlighting synchronized to the audio. The audio bar lets you adjust playback speed without re-fetching.

**Where do the Hebrew text and English translations come from?**

Sefaria's public API. The translation dropdown is populated automatically and defaults to JPS 1985 when available.

**Can I read without nikkud or cantillation marks?**

Yes. The settings drawer has separate toggles for nikkud (vowel points) and cantillation marks (te'amim). The cantillation strip uses Unicode range U+0591-U+05AF and leaves nikkud intact.

**Can it color-code the Torah trope (cantillation) families?**

Yes. Trope color coding tints each word by its cantillation clause family — Sof Pasuk, Zakef Katon, Segol, Revia, Geresh, and rare marks — with a legend above the reading. It composes with vowel color coding, keeps working when the cantillation marks themselves are hidden, and each family's color is customizable in settings.

**Does it work for both diaspora and Israel reading schedules?**

Yes. The default is diaspora; flip the Reading Schedule toggle in settings to switch to the Israel schedule. The 'Jump to this week's parsha' button fetches the current parsha from Sefaria using the chosen schedule.

**Can I copy the Hebrew text out of the reader?**

Yes. The Copy panel in the Options drawer copies the passage as rich text, keeping the vowel and trope colors, so it pastes into Google Docs, Word, or Pages. Copy one verse, select several, or type a verse range, and choose what travels with it — nikkud, cantillation marks, transliteration, translation, verse numbers, or blank lines for handwriting.

**Is the Torah Trainer free?**

Yes. Materials that incorporate PocketTorah audio are CC BY-SA 4.0; other IvritSuite content is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

## Trope Tutor

https://ivritsuite.com/trope_tutor.html

Learn the Torah cantillation marks (trope / te'amim) one clause family at a time — symbol, Ashkenazi and Sephardi names, and melody with real chanted examples — then drill yourself with three quiz modes and per-mark mastery tracking.

### How to learn the Torah trope (cantillation marks) with the Trope Tutor (about 5 minutes)

1. **Pick a clause family** — Start in Learn mode. The trope marks are grouped by clause family — use the chips above the cards to move between families.
2. **Study each mark's card** — Every card shows the mark's symbol on a Hebrew word plus its Ashkenazi and Sephardi names. Switch the primary naming tradition in settings.
3. **Play the chanted example** — Each card plays a real word from the Torah reading, clipped from PocketTorah's recordings, so you hear the mark's actual melody.
4. **Switch to Drill** — Drill sessions ask 10 questions of three kinds: name the trope on a marked word, hear a clip and pick the symbol, or pick the melody that matches a symbol.
5. **Track your mastery** — The per-mark mastery grid shows your progress. Marks you miss come up more often, and distractors get sneakier as your mastery grows.

### Questions

**What is the Trope Tutor?**

A free interactive tutor for the Torah cantillation marks (trope / te'amim). Learn mode teaches the marks one clause family at a time — symbol, names, and melody with real chanted examples — and Drill mode quizzes you three ways with per-mark mastery tracking.

**What melody tradition is this?**

The recordings are PocketTorah's, chanted in a widely-taught Ashkenazi melody. Both Ashkenazi and Sephardi trope names are shown, and you can switch the primary naming tradition in settings.

**What are trope (te'amim)?**

Cantillation marks printed above and below the words of the Hebrew Bible. Each mark names a melodic phrase and marks the grammar of the verse — together they tell you how to chant it.

**How does Drill mode work?**

Each session asks 10 questions of three kinds: see a marked word and name the trope, hear a clip and pick the symbol, or see a symbol and pick the matching melody. Marks you miss come up more often, and distractors get sneakier (like pashta vs. kadma) as your mastery grows.

**Where do the chanted examples come from?**

Every example is a real word from the Torah reading, clipped from PocketTorah's recordings (by Russel Neiss & Rabbi Charlie Schwartz, CC BY-SA 4.0) using their word-level timings. The Hebrew text comes from Sefaria.

**Is the Trope Tutor free?**

Yes. Materials that incorporate PocketTorah audio are CC BY-SA 4.0; other IvritSuite content is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. No account, no ads.

**Can I print a chart of all the trope marks?**

Yes. In Learn mode, the Print chart button prints all 26 marks as one reference sheet — each mark's symbol with its Ashkenazi and Sephardi names, grouped by clause family.

## Hebrew Font Maker

https://ivritsuite.com/Hebrew_Font_Maker.html

Make your own Hebrew fonts from your handwriting — trace or draw your letters — or open an existing font and edit it; place nikkud and trop, and export TrueType, WOFF2, or UFO.

### How to make a Hebrew font (about 20 minutes)

1. **Add your letters** — Add each Hebrew letter — one picture per letter, a full sheet, an existing font file, or drawn right in the browser.
2. **Trace** — The tool turns each picture into a clean outline; adjust the threshold and detail if needed.
3. **Anchor nikkud and trop** — Show where the vowel and cantillation marks sit on each letter.
4. **Export** — Download your finished font as TrueType (TTF), WOFF2, or UFO and install it.

### Questions

**Is the Hebrew Font Maker free?**

Yes. The Hebrew Font Maker is completely free — make and download as many Hebrew fonts as you like, with no account or sign-up.

**How do I make my own Hebrew font?**

Upload or scan a picture of each Hebrew letter — or draw it right in the browser — then trace it into an outline, place the nikkud and trop anchors, and export a real font you can install.

**Can I open and edit an existing Hebrew font?**

Yes. Import a TTF or OTF and the Font Maker brings across its letters, nikkud and trop — including each mark's own attachment position from the font's OpenType data — along with its English letters, punctuation and symbols. Edit what you like and export a new TrueType, WOFF2, or UFO file. Check the original font's license before redistributing anything based on it.

**Can I make free Hebrew fonts with nikkud and trop?**

Yes. The free Hebrew Font Maker positions nikkud (vowels) and cantillation (trop) automatically using OpenType mark positioning.

**What font formats can I export?**

TrueType (TTF), WOFF2 for the web, and editable UFO source — each with a license you choose (CC0, OFL, MIT, or All Rights Reserved).

**Do I need to install any software?**

No. The Hebrew Font Maker runs entirely in your browser; the font engine loads only when you export.

**How do I install a Hebrew font on Windows, Mac, or Google Docs?**

On Windows, double-click the downloaded .ttf file and choose Install. On Mac, double-click it and click Install Font in Font Book. Google Docs only uses fonts from its own catalog and cannot load a local font, so use a desktop word processor such as Word, Pages, or LibreOffice, or upload the file to a design tool like Canva instead.

**Are fonts I make here free to use commercially?**

That depends on the license you pick when you export. CC0 places the font in the public domain — free for any use, including commercial, with no attribution required. OFL and MIT are also free for commercial use under their terms. All Rights Reserved keeps the font yours to license as you wish. You own what you create; IvritSuite claims no rights to your fonts.

**Do the fonts include nikkud (vowels) and cantillation (trop)?**

Yes. As you build each letter you can anchor its nikkud and trop marks, and the exported font uses OpenType GPOS mark positioning so the marks land in the right place automatically as you type. You can also make a letters-only font and skip the marks.

## Hebrew Teaching Resources

https://ivritsuite.com/resources.html

Curated directory of external Hebrew and Jewish education resources, tools, and references.

### How to find Hebrew teaching resources

1. **Pick a category** — Choose a category — Lesson Planning, Printables, Tanakh, Hebrew, Culture, or Miscellaneous.
2. **Pick an age group** — Filter by age group — K-2, 3-5, 6-12, or Adult/Teacher.
3. **Open a resource** — Click any resource card to open it in a new tab.

### Questions

**What's in the Hebrew teaching resources directory?**

A curated set of websites, printables, lesson-planning tools, Tanakh references, Hebrew language sites, and Jewish culture resources, filterable by category and age group.

**Are all the linked resources free?**

Most listed resources are free; some link to paid or premium services. Each card notes if a resource requires registration or payment.

**Who is this directory for?**

Hebrew and Jewish-studies teachers, day-school faculty, supplementary-school teachers, parents, and adult learners looking for vetted Hebrew learning materials.
